A wharf berth registry caps voting power by physical space: signing rights require occupying one berth at a named inlet with a fixed berth count.

Each berth issues one signed arrival token per epoch, stamped by the wharf's single clock. Arrivals broadcast an echo ping; incumbents countersign only pings they saw in that inlet, so a fake identity cannot gather countersignatures without a real berth.

Cost: each puppet rents its own berth, paying full fee plus a surcharge rising with inlet occupancy. No bulk discount: N identities cost N full fees until berths run out; an honest agent pays once.
